what: The mirror of coverage-floors.json. That file records how much of the syllabus the
LESSONS reach; this one records how much of it any QUESTION names. Same term lists,
same matcher, so the two are directly comparable — and on the day this was written
That gap is the standing brief's fourth promise failing in the direction no gate
watched: LAW-47 proves whatever we test was taught first, and nothing proved that
what we taught is ever tested. A learner could finish every study set, sit the mock,
score well, and meet the real paper cold on two thirds of the syllabus.
these_are_a_ratchet_not_a_target: 35% is recorded because it is BAD. The floors exist so the number cannot silently
go down while the real target is 100%; they are not a standard anything has met.
This is deliberately NOT the mistake LAW-75 names. That law warns against calibrating
a defect DETECTOR on the population it polices, because a threshold drawn through
contaminated data sits exactly where the existing defects already are. A
set-membership ratchet makes no judgement about what is good — it only refuses to let
today's number drop — so contamination cannot hide inside it.
Raise a floor when authoring lands. Never lower one to make a run green.
how_to_use_the_misses: --triage splits every miss into three buckets, because they need different work:
drift    one question carries every distinctive word of the term, in another order.
Usually the bank naming the idea differently. A wording decision.
partial  some words land in one question. Read the item before deciding.
absent   no question comes close. Genuine authoring.
As measured 2026-08-18: 39 drift, 143 partial, 51 absent, across 233 misses.
The triage is measured PER QUESTION, not per corpus, and that correction matters.
The first version asked whether each word appeared anywhere in the subject's bank,
which across 236 questions is nearly free: 'Return on assets' was called drift
because 'return' appears 7 times and 'assets' 5 times in unrelated questions, while
the bank never says ROA or return on assets at all. It now reads partial, correctly.
scope_limit: This asks whether the bank NAMES an idea, not whether it tests it well — a single
mention in a distractor counts. A PASS means nothing regressed; it never means the
course is tested. Read the tool header before quoting a number from it.
raised: 2026-08-19: SPMS 30 -> 34. Six concept records added to module 1 — Physical vs software
products, Marginal cost, Embedded product, Product family, Product platform, Product line —
taking SPMS from 16 to 22 concepts. Each record generates its own surfaces, so those six
ideas went from untested to tested without a question being written by hand, which is the
whole argument for widening the spine before authoring questions one at a time.
Raised because authoring landed, exactly as the rule above says. The other three are
untouched.
2026-08-19: SCLM 33 -> 100. Twenty concept records authored across all eight modules, one per
lecture that no question had ever cited, plus one drift repair on sclm_fit so strategic fit uses
the course own terms (efficient supply chain, responsive supply chain, cost-responsiveness
frontier). SCLM concepts 16 -> 36 and questions 236 -> 516; every one of the 84 named ideas is
now reached. Authoring, not accounting: no alias was added and no floor was lowered.
2026-08-20: SPMS 34 -> 100. Forty-seven concept records were added after the module 1 pilot,
taking SPMS from 22 to 69 concepts and 300 to 958 questions. Every one of the 116 named ideas
is now reached, every concept has a generated neighbour link, and an authored roadmap/traceability
synthesis item supplies the subject's first cross-module edge. No syllabus alias or lowered floor.
2026-08-20: BRGSA 67 -> 100. Thirteen transcript-grounded concept records plus three honest
wording repairs took BRGSA from 16 to 29 concepts and 248 to 417 questions. All 69 named ideas
are reached; the legacy 60-question concept mapping retained the same SHA-256 digest before and
after widening. No syllabus alias was added and no floor was lowered.
2026-08-20: IBM 19 -> 100. The 73-idea queue became 69 new classified records and four
course-wording repairs on existing layer records: 20 layer ideas generate written plus MCQ
practice, 29 frameworks generate written practice only, and 20 atomic concepts generate MCQ
practice only. Together with the original sixteen layer records, IBM now has 85 concepts and
936 questions, including 167 constructed responses. All 90 named ideas are reached without
inventing the unreleased examination case, adding a syllabus alias, or lowering a floor.
